articles.title: Meloni: "Non può esserci pace in Ucraina senza l'Europa"
articles.summary: AGI - "A Dublino, noi leader abbiamo stabilito come accompagnare questo processo: un team europeo", nel cosiddetto formato E5, nel quale è presente l'Italia, "che lavora in stretta collaborazione con l'Ucraina e gli Stati Uniti. Ora dobbiamo conferire a questo team un mandato chiaro: cosa chiediamo, cosa offriamo e cosa non accetteremo mai". Così la presidente del Consiglio, Giorgia Meloni, si è rivolta ai partecipanti al vertice dei Volenterosi per l'Ucraina a Berlino. "E non ci presentiamo a mani vuote", ha sottolineato ancora la premier, "questa coalizione sta lavorando a garanzie di sicurezza, incluso l'impegno ispirato all'Articolo 5 proposto dall'Italia - un modello che ora si trova sul tavolo negoziale". Meloni: "Non può esserci pace senza l'Europa" "Oggi - ha continuato Meloni - i leader di Stati Uniti, Russia e Cina si sono incontrati a Shenzhen. La loro dichiarazione parla di stabilità strategica, energia e rischi nucleari. Accogliamo con favore l'impegno a evitare che una guerra nucleare venga mai combattuta. Tuttavia, nel testo non si fa menzione della guerra in Ucraina. Ciò ci suggerisce due cose. Primo: la Cina conta in questo conflitto e, se intende essere una forza di stabilità, questo è il momento di esercitare la propria influenza per spingere la Russia verso una pace reale. Secondo: è chiaro a tutti che non può esserci pace in Ucraina senza l'Ucraina. E non può esserci pace senza l'Europa". La pressione sulla Russia e gli attacchi alle infrastrutture energetiche Meloni ha poi osservato: "Quanto ai russi, francamente, non so cosa aspettarmi. Lo scambio di prigionieri concordato ad Abu Dhabi è un segnale positivo; accogliamo con favore ogni passo di natura umanitaria. Ma la vera prova consiste nell'interruzione verificabile degli attacchi alle infrastrutture energetiche". "A Shenzhen, i tre leader hanno ribadito l'importanza di flussi energetici stabili. Bene. Prendiamoli in parola, a cominciare dalla rete elettrica ucraina. È una questione che ci riguarda tutti: la sicurezza delle centrali nucleari nel nostro continente, milioni di civili che affrontano l'inverno, mercati energetici già sotto pressione. Se Mosca dovesse opporsi, il mondo vedrà chiaramente chi desidera la pace e chi no. Nel frattempo, continuiamo a sostenere l'Ucraina e a mantenere alta la pressione sulla Russia". "L'Italia - ha concluso Meloni - sta facendo la sua parte e continuerà a farla: abbiamo appena adottato un nuovo pacchetto di aiuti militari, proseguiremo il lavoro sulle garanzie, contribuiremo al team negoziale europeo e sosterremo la ricostruzione dell'Ucraina - un impegno che portiamo avanti sin dalla Conferenza sulla ricostruzione tenutasi a Roma". Gli Stati Uniti vogliono accelerare il percorso verso la pace Fonti italiane hanno poi riferito che "gli Stati Uniti hanno ribadito la volontà di arrivare il prima possibile a una pace in Ucraina", sottolineando che "è emersa una volontà da parte di tutti di cogliere un momentum che si crede, si pensa essere particolarmente favorevole", con Washington intenzionata a imprimere un'accelerazione al percorso verso una soluzione del conflitto e gli europei chiamati a dare concretezza al proprio contributo. Non soltanto sul piano economico, ma anche attraverso un'agenda politica e negoziale definita, sulla quale si continuerà a lavorare a livello di consiglieri, insieme agli inviati speciali americani e ucraini. Il siparietto con Merz e il colloquio con Kushner Meloni ha lasciato il summit al termine dei lavori per volare a Roma e collegarsi con gli altri leader di centrodestra per fare il punto sulla manovra. Al suo arrivo in Cancelleria, dove si è svolto il summit, la premier è stata protagonista di un simpatico siparietto: l'auto su cui viaggiava non si è fermata davanti al tappeto rosso allestito dal cerimoniale, ma solo qualche metro più avanti, e ha dovuto fare una breve retromarcia. "Giorgia, vai troppo veloce", ha scherzato Merz prima di abbracciarla e stringerle la mano. A margine della foto di famiglia, la premier ha avuto anche un breve colloquio con Jared Kushner, uno dei due inviati Usa per l'Ucraina, nonché genero di Trump.

articles.title: Il principe Harry: 'Mi riarruolerei per combattere contro la Russia'
articles.summary: Al Telegraph: 'Gb in conflitto con Mosca ormai da un decennio'
articles.preview: Il principe Harry è pronto a rimettere la divisa, se il Regno Unito dovesse averne bisogno di fronte alla "minaccia" della Russia. A undici anni dal congedo, il duca di Sussex si è detto disposto a riarruolarsi nelle Forze armate britanniche in un'intervista esclusiva al podcast del Telegraph 'Ukraine: The Latest', registrata a Leopoli durante la sua visita a sorpresa in Ucraina dello scorso fine settimana.
articles.body:
Il principe Harry è pronto a rimettere la divisa, se il Regno Unito dovesse averne bisogno di fronte alla "minaccia" della Russia. A undici anni dal congedo, il duca di Sussex si è detto disposto a riarruolarsi nelle Forze armate britanniche in un'intervista esclusiva al podcast del Telegraph 'Ukraine: The Latest', registrata a Leopoli durante la sua visita a sorpresa in Ucraina dello scorso fine settimana.

"Se mi venisse chiesto di arruolarmi nuovamente, qualora ce ne fosse bisogno, sarei disponibile al 100% per servire il mio Paese al fianco dei miei commilitoni reduci e del personale militare in servizio", ha dichiarato il secondogenito di re Carlo III. Durante la visita, la quarta dall'inizio della guerra con la Russia, Harry aveva assistito alle selezioni della squadra ucraina per gli Invictus Games, da lui creati, promettendo ai militari feriti di sostenere Kiev nell'organizzazione dell'evento quando "l'Ucraina avrà vinto".

Il principe si è riferito nello specifico alla situazione del Paese invaso, per cui già in passato non ha nascosto un forte supporto, sostenendo che "c'è molto da imparare". E ha aggiunto che, a suo parere, anche il Regno Unito in realtà è in conflitto con Mosca ormai da un decennio. "Solo perché non ci sono droni, proiettili e razzi che ci volano addosso, non significa che non siamo in guerra", è la sua considerazione.

Secondo Harry, "l'Europa ha preso coscienza della minaccia" rappresentata dalla Russia, ma il suo "maggiore timore" è che il continente possa "dividersi". Interpellato sulla situazione geopolitica attuale, ha risposto: "Penso che dovremmo essere tutti preoccupati, assolutamente. E penso che dovremmo essere preparati e che coloro tra noi che hanno prestato servizio dovrebbero essere pronti a farlo nuovamente". Il principe ha esortato a "raddoppiare il nostro sostegno" per Kiev invece di fare un passo indietro, pur osservando che "serve una qualche forma di strategia d'uscita per la Russia".

Senza nominare Donald Trump, ha inoltre criticato l'approccio della Casa Bianca, sottolineando la "grande separazione" tra il sostegno all'Ucraina della società americana e la linea di "un'amministrazione" che "forse la pensava diversamente". Harry aveva già prestato servizio nell'esercito per circa dieci anni, completando due turni in Afghanistan, il secondo dei quali come pilota di elicotteri Apache, prima del congedo arrivato nel 2015.

articles.title: Nearly a quarter of the world’s children live in conflict zones, according to Save the Children
articles.summary: A 'record rate' of 589 million children were living in war zones in 2025, with 44% of them in Africa.
articles.preview: Nearly a quarter of the world's children are currently living in a conflict zone, a record rate since statistics were first recorded in the 1990s, the charity Save the Children said on Thursday, November 19. "Almost one in four children worldwide are now living in conflict zones, the highest number since records began in 1990," the London-based charity said. "The figure represents an increase of more than 50% in a decade, jumping from 378 million in 2015 to 589 million in 2025," it added.
articles.body:
Nearly a quarter of the world's children are currently living in a conflict zone, a record rate since statistics were first recorded in the 1990s, the charity Save the Children said on Thursday, November 19.

"Almost one in four children worldwide are now living in conflict zones, the highest number since records began in 1990," the London-based charity said. "The figure represents an increase of more than 50% in a decade, jumping from 378 million in 2015 to 589 million in 2025," it added.

The report was titled "Stop the War on Children: Changing the Odds" and drew on statistics from the Peace Research Institute Oslo (PRIO). The percentage of children living in conflict zones has doubled from 10% in the mid-1990s to 23.4% in 2025.

"These record-high figures are a stark reminder that conflict is devastating the daily lives, education, health and future prospects of hundreds of millions of children," said Gudrun Ostby, a research professor at PRIO. "Unless greater efforts are made to protect children in conflict settings, the consequences of today's wars will be felt for decades to come," he added.

The report defines conflict zones as areas existing within a 50-kilometer radius in which at least one armed attack took place. Africa has the largest number of children living in conflict zones, at about 260 million, or 44% of the total across the globe, the report found.

Rates have surged in the Middle East as well, from 52 million children in 2024 to 67 million in 2025, a 29% increase. An average of two in five children in Africa and the Middle East are living in conflict zones, it added.

"The scale of this crisis is rapidly growing, and the systems meant to protect children are being pushed to breaking point," said Inger Ashing, chief executive of Save The Children International.

articles.summary: Hamas condemned the incursion, which the Israeli military said was to dismantle a "terror tunnel", as a "flagrant" ceasefire violation.
articles.preview: Israeli forces have completed a rare ground operation in part of central Gaza outside their control, the military says, a day after residents were ordered to evacuate. Families fled their homes and tents on Wednesday as tanks advanced into an area east of Nuseirat refugee camp and onto the territory's main north-south road under the cover of artillery strikes. articles.body:
Israeli forces have completed a rare ground operation in part of central Gaza outside their control, the military says, a day after residents were ordered to evacuate.

Families fled their homes and tents on Wednesday as tanks advanced into an area east of Nuseirat refugee camp and onto the territory's main north-south road under the cover of artillery strikes.

The Israeli military said the "targeted" operation aimed to dismantle a "terror tunnel" west of the so-called Yellow Line, which marks the more than 60% of Gaza's territory occupied by Israel.

The Palestinian armed group Hamas, which controls the rest of Gaza, accused Israel of a "flagrant violation" of the October 2025 ceasefire deal.

Violence has continued in Gaza over the past 13 months, with near-daily Israeli strikes, and living conditions for the 2.1 million people there remain dire.

Wednesday's Israeli incursion deep beyond the Yellow Line was reportedly the first to be publicly announced by the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) since the ceasefire began.

In the early afternoon, Israeli military body Cogat's Arabic spokesperson announced the start of the operation and warned Palestinians living in an area north of Nuseirat and Bureij refugee camp to stay away for their own safety. It also said a section of Salah al-Din road that passed through the area would be closed to traffic.

In the evening, the IDF said the joint operation with the Shin Bet security service sought "to dismantle a terror tunnel west of the Yellow Line that posed an immediate and direct threat to IDF troops".

On Thursday morning, Cogat told Palestinians on social media that "the activity has ended, and the Salah al-Din axis has been reopened".

Hamas warned in a statement that the advance of Israeli military vehicles beyond the Yellow Line and the evacuation of residents constituted "a dangerous development and a flagrant violation of the ceasefire agreement".

Gaza's Hamas-run government media office meanwhile said that an estimated 6,000 people had fled their homes and tents because of the operation, and that this amounted to the war crime of forced displacement.

Footage published by Palestinian media outlets and on social media showed dozens of families fleeing areas near Nuseirat camp following the Israeli evacuation order.

In one video verified by BBC Verify, a man could be seen ducking after hearing artillery fire and then running along Salah al-Din road, about 1.5km (0.9 miles) west of the Yellow Line. "The Israeli occupation now is firing randomly near the houses and tents of people," he said.

An image, meanwhile, showed six armoured vehicles, including tanks and bulldozers, around Salah al-Din road.

A resident of Nuseirat who was forced to flee told BBC Arabic's Middle East Daily programme: "The situation is now extremely dire, with Israeli forces firing indiscriminately at areas where displaced people have sought shelter."

"We couldn't take any of our belongings with us - not even our blankets, pillows, or clothes. We had no choice but to leave everything behind."

A second resident also reported "indiscriminate gunfire and shelling" and said there had been "numerous casualties, including fatalities".

Asked about those reports, the IDF sent a general statement about the operation.

Multiple verified videos of the aftermath of the incursion on Thursday showed destruction, earth banks, and heavy vehicle tracks more than 1.2km beyond the Yellow Line.

That is believed to be the furthest Israeli troops have advanced into central Gaza since they occupied the so-called Netzarim Corridor before the ceasefire.

Some residents returned to check their properties following the Israeli withdrawal.

"The entire area has been destroyed, and we honestly do not know what to do," Abd Aliwa told Reuters news agency as he sat beside a pile of rubble.

- Israel moves Yellow Line deeper into Gaza, satellite images show

- Published16 January

Gaza's Hamas-run Civil Defence agency said three people were killed and others were wounded in three separate Israeli drone strikes on Wednesday.

One man was killed in Nuseirat, the second was killed to the north in Gaza City, and the third was killed in the central town of Deir al-Balah, it added.

The IDF told the BBC that it had "struck several military operatives".

Gaza health officials said another two people were killed on Thursday by Israeli fire in eastern Gaza City, according to Reuters. There was no immediate comment from the IDF.

At least 1,662 people have been killed in Israeli attacks in Gaza since the ceasefire began last year, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.

The Israeli military says six of its soldiers have been killed over the same period.

Meanwhile, more than 1.9 million people - about 90% of Gaza's population - remain displaced, with 1.4 million of them living in tents or makeshift shelters, according to the UN.

Reconstruction has yet to begin in Gaza, where an estimated 82% of all structures have been destroyed or damaged during the war, as US President Donald Trump's peace plan has largely stalled.

The disarmament of Hamas has been a key sticking point.

The group has agreed to give up its weapons in exchange for a phased withdrawal of Israeli troops from the 60% of Gaza they currently occupy. But Israel has insisted that Hamas must fully disarm before any pullout.

The war was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, when about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others were taken hostage.

Since then, more than 74,710 people have been killed in Israeli attacks in Gaza, its health ministry says.

articles.title: Xi, Trump y Putin, tras la cumbre de Shenzhen: “Una guerra nuclear no se puede ganar y nunca debe librarse”
articles.summary: Los líderes de las tres mayores potencias se comprometen a reformar la ONU y a garantizar los flujos energéticos. El republicano se refiere al mandatario ruso como “amigo”
articles.preview: Los líderes de las tres mayores potencias se comprometen a reformar la ONU y a garantizar los flujos energéticos. El republicano se refiere al mandatario ruso como “amigo” Xi Jinping pidió este jueves que las tres potencias nucleares den ejemplo en la defensa de la paz mundial, con Vladímir Putin a su derecha y Donald Trump a su izquierda. Entenderse es una “obligación ineludible”, afirmó el presidente chino al tiempo que proponía mantener contactos regulares al más alto nivel y crear un mecanismo trilateral para evitar crisis.
articles.body:
Los líderes de las tres mayores potencias se comprometen a reformar la ONU y a garantizar los flujos energéticos. El republicano se refiere al mandatario ruso como “amigo”

Xi Jinping pidió este jueves que las tres potencias nucleares den ejemplo en la defensa de la paz mundial, con Vladímir Putin a su derecha y Donald Trump a su izquierda. Entenderse es una “obligación ineludible”, afirmó el presidente chino al tiempo que proponía mantener contactos regulares al más alto nivel y crear un mecanismo trilateral para evitar crisis. Una fricción menor, advirtió, puede convertirse en un gran conflicto si los dirigentes dejan de hablarse.

Los mandatarios de China, Estados Unidos y Rusia, que ya se habían reunido por separado, se han sentado esta vez a la misma mesa en una cumbre histórica, la primera a tres bandas entre los jefes de Estado de estas naciones. La reunión, que ha durado una hora y 20 minutos, se ha celebrado en los márgenes de la cumbre del Foro de Cooperación Económica Asia-Pacífico (APEC) en Shenzhen, completamente eclipsada por esta cita inédita.

“Cuando las grandes potencias viven en armonía, el mundo está en paz. Cuando se enfrentan, el mundo cae en el caos”, ha afirmado Xi en la ciudad meridional china. Según la lectura oficial del encuentro difundida por Pekín, los tres países se han comprometido a impulsar la reforma de la ONU y han acordado mantener un diálogo para reducir los riesgos nucleares y evitar la proliferación. “Una guerra nuclear no se puede ganar y nunca debe librarse”, se lee en el comunicado.

Pekín, Moscú y Washington prevén, siempre según la versión china, aumentar la producción y el suministro de combustibles fósiles y garantizar la estabilidad de los flujos energéticos. También reconocen la “importancia fundamental del principio del consentimiento de los Estados” y del “respeto a la inmunidad de la que gozan los funcionarios estatales”, y coinciden en que el Tribunal Penal Internacional y otros organismos similares “no deben abusar de su jurisdicción”.

Para Trump, el hecho mismo de que los tres se hayan sentado a hablar es motivo de celebración: “Nunca se ha forjado la paz dejando pasar las oportunidades del diálogo. Estamos realmente haciendo historia”, ha declarado en los primeros minutos de la reunión. “Con la vieja práctica de negarse a hablar de los problemas, jamás se resolvió uno”.

La Casa Blanca ha calificado la reunión de “encuentro sin precedentes en la escena internacional”. El ministro de Exteriores chino, Wang Yi, ha afirmado que ha sido un hito “con repercusiones de gran alcance para las relaciones internacionales”. “Nadie esperaba que todo saliera tan bien”, le ha confiado un Putin exultante a su anfitrión al término de la reunión, según los medios rusos.

La gran incógnita era si la guerra en Ucrania figuraría en la agenda. Para el anfitrión, es un asunto delicado. Xi quiere preservar su estrecha relación con Moscú, mientras que los dirigentes europeos, con los que China mantiene importantes vínculos comerciales, le reclaman que ejerza su fuerza sobre Putin para que ponga fin a la guerra. A los líderes de Ucrania y la Unión Europea les preocupa que Trump alcance un acuerdo con Putin sin ni siquiera la presencia de Kiev en las negociaciones. En estos más de cuatro años y medio de conflicto, Pekín lo califica como una mera “crisis”.

Finalmente, la Casa Blanca ha incluido la cuestión, así como la reducción de los arsenales nucleares y la defensa de la soberanía nacional frente a lo que Trump ha llamado “organizaciones globalistas”, entre ellas el Tribunal Penal Internacional (TPI). “Está fuera de control”, ha dicho el estadounidense de ese órgano, al que acusa de “extralimitarse en sus competencias” y al que su Administración ha sometido a un intenso acoso.

El TPI ha dictado sendas órdenes de detención contra Putin, por la presunta deportación y traslado ilegal de menores ucranios, y contra el primer ministro israelí y aliado clave de Trump, Benjamín Netanyahu, por presuntos crímenes de guerra y lesa humanidad en Gaza.

En declaraciones posteriores a la prensa, Putin ha calificado la reunión de “abierta” y “muy útil”, y ha afirmado que el presidente chino logró crear un clima que permitió a los tres dirigentes intercambiar puntos de vista con libertad. “Nos ha ayudado a entendernos mejor”, ha señalado. Sobre Ucrania, ha dicho que Kiev y Bruselas aún no están dispuestos a hacer concesiones para poner fin al conflicto. También ha asegurado haber enviado invitaciones a las capitales europeas, a través de canales diplomáticos, para que sus representantes viajen a Moscú para aclarar sus posiciones.

Xi ha sido el único de los tres que no ha mencionado a Ucrania en lo que ha trascendido de su intervención. Trump, por su parte, ha denominado el conflicto como “la guerra entre Rusia y Ucrania”, obviando el papel invasor de Moscú.

El dirigente estadounidense también ha aprovechado la cita para plantear a sus homólogos que debatan cómo reducir el número de armas nucleares y el riesgo de que lleguen a emplearse, y ha citado a Teherán al reclamar su cooperación para frenar la proliferación. “No vamos a dejar que Irán tenga un arma nuclear”, ha enfatizado. Tanto Rusia como China han aportado apoyo de diversa índole a la República Islámica durante el conflicto bélico que la enfrenta a EE UU e Israel, sea comprando petróleo o suministrándole material de doble uso. Xi ha recurrido a la imagen de una “espada de Damocles” que pende sobre la humanidad para defender ante Trump y Putin que “una guerra nuclear no se puede ganar y jamás debe librarse”.

Durante la reunión, Xi ha evocado la lucha de China, la Unión Soviética y EE UU contra el fascismo en la II Guerra Mundial para reclamar a las tres potencias que cooperen también hoy. Por su parte, Putin ha recordado el papel de los tres países en la fundación de Naciones Unidas y ha sostenido que comparten la responsabilidad de preservar la paz y defender los principios de la Carta de la ONU.

“¿Qué tuvo de malo Yalta?”, ha preguntado Putin a la prensa. “En Yalta quedó consagrada la victoria sobre el nazismo... no me importaría que se consagrara también una victoria sobre el neonazismo. De hecho, me parecería lo correcto”, ha zanjado. “En Yalta nadie se repartió el mundo. Allí simplemente se dejó constancia de la realidad que había surgido tras la II Guerra Mundial. Y en los conflictos actuales, habrá que aceptar la realidad sobre el terreno”, ha afirmado Putin, en lo que parece una alusión velada a Ucrania. “Gracias a aquellos acuerdos [que alumbraron la ONU], el mundo ha vivido sin grandes convulsiones mundiales. Ha habido muchos conflictos regionales, sí, pero ninguno de alcance mundial”, prosiguió.

El escenario elegido para esta cumbre en los márgenes de la APEC es la villa de Kylin, en el noroeste de Shenzhen. Xi los ha recibido en un amplio salón presidido por una gran mesa redonda, en la que han estado sentados a solas; las respectivas delegaciones han seguido la conversación a cierta distancia. Detrás de Xi, una gigantesca pintura tradicional decoraba la estancia. En ella aparecía la Gran Muralla china entre un paisaje de montañas, pinos y nubes. En su cultura, las montañas simbolizan la estabilidad, los pinos se consideran una forma de dar la bienvenida a los invitados y representan la longevidad, y la Gran Muralla alude a la fuerza nacional.

La villa Kylin es un complejo de cinco estrellas que las autoridades locales utilizan desde 1997 para recibir a dirigentes chinos y extranjeros, una función similar a la de Diaoyutai en Pekín. Sus edificios de estilo europeo se reparten entre jardines, cerca de el embalse de Xili, del zoológico de la ciudad y de un campo de golf. Para el presidente chino, tiene un significado especial: allí pasó parte de sus últimos meses de vida su padre, el revolucionario Xi Zhongxun. Según cuenta su biografía oficial, publicada en 2013 y escrita por historiadores del Partido Comunista, Xi Zhongxun frecuentaba esta villa para descansar y pasear por recomendación de sus médicos tras ser diagnosticado de cáncer.

Shezhen, símbolo de apertura

Para Xi, haber conseguido que Trump y Putin acepten esa cita ya es un éxito diplomático en sí. Durante décadas, Washington y sus aliados occidentales marcaron en gran medida las reglas del orden internacional. Esta vez, es China la que reúne a los presidentes de EE UU y de Rusia, y lo hace en Shenzhen, la ciudad que simboliza su apertura económica y donde hoy circulan coches autónomos por sus calles y drones reparten pedidos. Al convocar a ambos dirigentes en el marco de un foro económico, Xi busca mostrar que el ascenso comercial y tecnológico de su país le ha dado también mayor peso en la política mundial.

“[Es] una imagen impactante de un orden que gira en torno a China, una suerte de G-3 presidido por Xi”, escribe Julian Gewirtz, exdirector para China del Consejo de Seguridad Nacional de EE UU durante la Administración de Joe Biden. “Este triángulo no tiene nada de equilátero. Xi se ha situado en el vértice superior”.

Antes de la reunión a tres bandas, los presidentes de la primera y segunda economía del planeta habían tratado su propia relación bilateral. En ese encuentro, Trump aseguró que coinciden en que el petróleo debe volver a circular por el estrecho de Ormuz, sobre el que hoy pesa un doble bloqueo: estadounidense e iraní.

Xi, por su parte, ha pedido a Trump que EE UU “siga haciendo lo correcto” respecto a la cuestión de Taiwán para evitar “grandes reveses” en la relación entre Pekín y Washington, la cual, ha reconocido, se ha mantenido estable y ha mejorado. Según la versión de Pekín, Trump ha respondido que EE UU no apoya la independencia de la isla, que está gobernada democráticamente y que China reclama como parte irrenunciable de su territorio. Es la tercera reunión bilateral entre ambos mandatarios este año, tras las de Pekín, en mayo, y Washington, en septiembre. Trump ha puesto el acento en el trato personal que mantienen: “El presidente Xi y yo hemos forjado una relación personal extraordinaria. De verdad. A algunos les disgusta oírlo, pero yo estoy muy contento”.

En el terreno comercial, Trump ha pedido “que haga algo más por nuestros agricultores, porque China tiene un apetito insaciable”. El comunicado chino señala que Xi ha pedido más diálogo para resolver las diferencias comerciales. La tregua pactada entre ambos países expira el próximo 10 de enero.

“Putin es mi amigo”

Trump se había visto previamente durante 40 minutos con Putin, al final de la reunión plenaria de los líderes del APEC. “¿Quién es?... Es mi amigo”, bromeó el republicano antes de estrecharle la mano, darle una palmada en la espalda e inclinarse para susurrarle algo al oído. Putin sonreía.

Ambos ya se habían saludado la víspera en presencia del anfitrión de la cumbre, poco antes del gran banquete de bienvenida en el que estuvieron presentes los representantes de los países que conforman el foro. Era la primera vez que ambos mantenían un encuentro personal desde su cita en Alaska, en agosto del pasado año.

articles.title: Putin vows 'far more painful' response to Ukraine's strikes on Crimean Bridge
articles.summary: The bridge - a symbol of Russia's occupation of the Crimean Peninsula - suffered major damaged following a combined attack by Ukraine earlier this week.
articles.preview: Moscow's retaliation for attacks on the Crimean Bridge will be "far more painful" than Kyiv's strikes, Vladimir Putin has vowed. In the early hours of Thursday, the double-arched, 12-mile bridge connecting Russia to Ukraine's occupied peninsula of Crimea was hit for a third time this week. A combined missile-and-drone strike on Tuesday destroyed the central road section of the bridge, collapsing part of it into the water and rendering it unusable for road traffic.
articles.body:
Moscow's retaliation for attacks on the Crimean Bridge will be "far more painful" than Kyiv's strikes, Vladimir Putin has vowed.

In the early hours of Thursday, the double-arched, 12-mile bridge connecting Russia to Ukraine's occupied peninsula of Crimea was hit for a third time this week.

A combined missile-and-drone strike on Tuesday destroyed the central road section of the bridge, collapsing part of it into the water and rendering it unusable for road traffic.

But at a press conference after historic talks with his Chinese and US counterparts in Shenzhen, Russian president Putin said Moscow's response would be even more significant.

Putin claimed the bridge was used exclusively for civilian purposes and not to transport military equipment, as Kyiv has alleged, or petroleum products.

Since illegally annexing the Crimean Peninsula in 2014, Moscow has used it as a military base, with airbases, troop concentrations, training grounds and artillery stockpiles.

From there it has also carried out strikes on the rest of the country and resupplied its troops in southern Ukraine.

Commenting on the strikes on the bridge, Kyiv's defence ministry said that for Ukraine, they amounted to to "time gained and lives saved. The less that reaches the occupiers, the less hits our warriors."

The collapse of the Crimean Bridge's arch was the worst damage to be inflicted onto the structure in several years.

The bridge had long been in Ukraine's sights because it represents Moscow's pretensions over sovereign Ukrainian land, and because of its logistical importance in supplying Russian troops in the occupied Ukrainian southern regions.

It was built and unveiled to great fanfare in 2018, four years after Russia illegally annexed Ukraine's Crimea.

Thursday's strike was carried out with Neptune cruise missiles, Ukraine said. Russia's transport ministry said nobody had been hurt in the attack, and that specialists were assessing damage to the bridge. Train services on the bridge were suspended but resumed in the afternoon.

Car traffic, however, will be prohibited for the foreseeable future as a section about 200m (660ft) long of the tarmac was dragged below into the sea when missiles hit the arch on Tuesday.

President Volodymyr Zelensky called the initial strikes on the Crimean Bridge an "unprecedented operation" weeks in the making.

The seven-stage operation first required the destruction of air defence systems, radars, electronic warfare assets which protected the bridge. Missiles and drones then dealt the structure the final blow.

In response to Tuesday's hit, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the bridge "will be rebuilt, and it will be even better than before".

But the operation to repair it could take a long time, and it will likely have to be carried out under frequent Ukrainian fire.

Russia has regularly targeted Ukrainian civilian infrastructure since launching its full-scale invasion in 2022.

This week alone, as the Crimean Bridge was being hit, Moscow targeted key bridge crossings over the Dnipro River in Kyiv.

articles.title: Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya, top UN court rules
articles.summary: The International Court of Justice has upheld large parts of a genocide case against Myanmar linked to the 2017 conflict with its Rohingya minority. It called for it to pay reparations and let refugees return safely.
articles.preview: November 19, 2026 The International Court of Justice has upheld large parts of a genocide case against Myanmar linked to the 2017 conflict with its Rohingya minority. It called for it to pay reparations and let refugees return safely. The International Court of Justice (ICJ) on Thursday found Myanmar in breach of several of its obligations under international treaties to prevent and not to commit genocide.
articles.body:
November 19, 2026

The International Court of Justice has upheld large parts of a genocide case against Myanmar linked to the 2017 conflict with its Rohingya minority. It called for it to pay reparations and let refugees return safely.

The International Court of Justice (ICJ) on Thursday found Myanmar in breach of several of its obligations under international treaties to prevent and not to commit genocide.

The ICJ's president, Judge Yuji Iwasawa said that the panel of 15 judges had decided by nine votes to six that Myanmar had committed genocide against the Rohingya in Rakhine state.

The judges also found the country guilty of a series of other more specific violations by majority rulings.

"On the basis of all the evidence taken together, the Court is of the view that the only reasonable inference that can explain Myanmar's actions is an intention to destroy a substantial part of... the Rohingya population in northern Rakhine State," ICJ President Yuji Iwasawa said.

Iwasawa said that Myanmar should make efforts to pay reparations to victims or their associates where possible and appropriate.

He also called for it to facilitate the safe return of refugees, and to take measures to investigate and, if necessary, prosecute individual wrongdoing by its nationals and security forces.

What Judge Iwasawa said as he read out the verdict against Myanmar

The ICJ said in its consideration, the Rohingya constituted a distinct ethnic group with their own defining language and culture, as well as self-identifying as such. This means they qualified as a protected group for the purposes of international laws against genocide.

Myanmar's security forces "killed thousands of Rohingya civilians, perpetrated acts of sexual violence, as well as extreme violence against children," and also attacked Rohingya as they tried to flee the fighting, the ICJ's Iwasawa said.

"The court is fully convinced that the 2017 clearance operations caused serious bodily and mental harm to a significant number of the protected group," Judge Iwasawa said.

Iwasawa also said that some civilian participation in the clearance operations could not necessarily be considered state-ordered or state-sanctioned behavior. But the court found that the government and security forces also made no meaningful efforts to prevent non-Rohingya civilian atrocities and fanned the flames of ethnic and religious tension.

At one point, reading the details of the findings, Iwasawa noted "Myanmar's failure, genuinely to investigate the alleged atrocities, and its refusal to facilitate access to evidence and witnesses, or provide information requested."

He said this meant it was possible the court did not have reliable knowledge of information available only from within Myanmar to which it was not given access.

How did groups from Myanmar respond?

There was no immediate response from the government in Myanmar or the military, which is regarded as the real underlying power.

Rohingya activist Yasmin Ullah — a Canadian citizen since 2016 but who was born in Rakhine state and who was a member of Gambia's delegation that filed the ICJ case — called the verdict more important for the world than for her community.

"The Rohingya never needed a court to tell us what happened to us," she said. "We needed the world to hear it, and today it has."

Wai Wai Nu, a Rohingya activist who directs the Women's Peace Network NGO, said the world's highest court's finding followed "decades" when "the Burmese military tried to erase our identity, deny our existence and dismiss our suffering."

And the co-chair of the Arakan Rohingya National Council, Nay San Lwin, said that for Rohingya people, "justice means the restoration of our citizenship, recognition of our identity and our safe and dignified return home."

Myanmar's shadow national unity government, which includes remnants of former President Aung San Suu Kyi's National League for Democracy Party, said it "respects the authority" of the ICJ.

It said that since the beginning of the "revolution against military dictatorship" in 2021, it had affirmed its "commitment to the rule of law, human rights, justice and states' obligations to prevent and punish genocide."

Myanmar was under nominally civilian rule at the time of the atrocities, but the extent to which Suu Kyi's government held sway over the military and its actions is debatable.

How did the international community react?

UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres welcomed Thursday's verdict, calling it a "powerful recognition of the Rohingya victims of genocide" and noting it was the first verdict of its kind against a state.

"Myanmar must act in accordance with its obligation to comply with the Court's decision," Guterres said in a statement, adding that this includes "the safe, voluntary and dignified return [of Rohingya] to their place of residence nad reunification of families."

Gambia's Justice Minister Dawda Jallow, who attended the hearing, spoke to reporters afterward at the Peace Palace in The Hague.

"The victory belongs to the Rohingya," Jallow said. "They survived. They testified. And today, they will believe."

UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband issued a statement saying the former colonial power was "taking immediate action today in light of this judgment."

Miliband said Britain would expel Myanmar's defense attache in London and was calling for a special UN Security Council session in response. He called on Myanmar to "comply fully with the judgment," and on the international community to "play its part in supporting implementation, accountability, and justice for the Rohingya."

UN human rights chief Volker Türk said the ruling "clearly concludes the State of Myanmar stands responsible for one of the most egregious crimes known to humankind."

What is the genocide case against Myanmar?

The case centers around the military crackdown in Rakhine state on the country's western coastline against the predominantly Muslim Rohingya minority in 2017.

Violence had been brewing for several years beforehand, but the most intense phase of the military crackdown in the north of region was triggered by a coordinated attack by a Muslim militia group against several police and military installations and personnel in August 2017.

A UN fact finding mission later concluded that some 10,000 people likely died in the military clearance operations that followed. Around 700,000 people fled to Bangladesh, where most still reside in the world's largest refugee camp.

Gambia filed the complaint at The Hague in 2019, alleging a deliberate campaign of arson, rape and murder designed to wipe out the Rohingya minority in whole or in part.

Myanmar's influential military, now back in full de facto control of the country albeit amid a long-running civil war, has maintained that it was engaged in a legitimate counterinsurgency.

Aung San Suu Kyi, who was the civilian president at the time, took a slightly more nuanced stance, but nevertheless traveled to The Hague to contest the charges, calling them "incomplete and incorrect."

The case is likely to draw close attention from those pursuing ICJ prosecutions against Israel and Benjamin Netanyahu for the war in Gaza and against Russia and Vladimir Putin for the invasion of Ukraine.

articles.title: I primi cento giorni di El Tigre
articles.summary: Da agosto il presidente colombiano di estrema destra Abelardo de la Espriella ha dichiarato guerra ai gruppi criminali con metodi discutibili e ha represso il dissenso
articles.preview: Con la pistola alla cintura e il walkie-talkie in mano, il presidente colombiano Abelardo de la Espriella marcia insieme alle forze di sicurezza durante le retate notturne. I presunti criminali, fatti sfilare in manette, sono senza parole. Il nuovo sceriffo della Colombia li schernisce, poi li spedisce in prigione con una delle sue frasi tipiche: “Bienvenido a la patria milagro”, benvenuto nel paese del miracolo. I video pubblicati sui canali social del presidente offrono uno spettacolo gratificante per i colombiani esasperati dalla violenza.
articles.body:
Con la pistola alla cintura e il walkie-talkie in mano, il presidente colombiano Abelardo de la Espriella marcia insieme alle forze di sicurezza durante le retate notturne. I presunti criminali, fatti sfilare in manette, sono senza parole. Il nuovo sceriffo della Colombia li schernisce, poi li spedisce in prigione con una delle sue frasi tipiche: “Bienvenido a la patria milagro”, benvenuto nel paese del miracolo.

I video pubblicati sui canali social del presidente offrono uno spettacolo gratificante per i colombiani esasperati dalla violenza. De la Espriella, un populista di estrema destra che si fa chiamare El Tigre, ha promesso il pugno di ferro e una crescita vertiginosa. Dopo cento giorni di mandato, ha dato il via a entrambe le cose. Ma ci vorrà molto più di qualche video su TikTok per spezzare l’influenza che i gruppi armati esercitano su vaste aree del paese e per affrontare la crisi fiscale della Colombia. Nel frattempo, i suoi istinti autoritari lo hanno messo in rotta di collisione con il congresso e i tribunali. E la coalizione di sinistra che ha perso le elezioni per meno di un punto percentuale sta incoraggiando le persone a scendere in piazza.

Contenuti grotteschi

Il governo è entrato in carica in un momento di calamità. Il 10 agosto, tre giorni dopo la cerimonia d’insediamento, un terremoto ha colpito la Colombia uccidendo più di 300 persone e provocando danni per più di 13 miliardi di dollari. Il presidente e i suoi ministri hanno visitato le zone del disastro e hanno promesso un “fondo miracolo” per la ricostruzione (che ha tardato a concretizzarsi). Durante il governo del predecessore Gustavo Petro (di sinistra), i gruppi armati si sono espansi, la sicurezza è peggiorata e la produzione di cocaina ha raggiunto nuovi livelli record. De la Espriella ha abbandonato i colloqui di pace avviati da Petro, ha intensificato i bombardamenti contro i gruppi armati, ha fatto uccidere vari criminali di alto rango e ha autorizzato l’estradizione di altri negli Stati Uniti. Tutto questo è raccontato in un flusso quotidiano di contenuti online autocelebrativi, alcuni grotteschi.

Anche se molti colombiani sembrano apprezzare queste iniziative, l’aumento effettivo delle operazioni contro la criminalità è stato “modesto”, spiega Javier Flórez, del centro studi Fundación ideas para la paz. “In sostanza è sempre la stessa cosa: arresti, uccisioni, sequestri”. Servirà una strategia diversa per spezzare il potere dei criminali che dominano alcune zone della Colombia.

Il governo vuole nuovi strumenti per colpire i nemici. Una legge da poco in vigore, chiamata di sottomissione alla giustizia, offre pene ridotte ai criminali che confessano, consegnano i propri beni e collaborano con la giustizia, ma esclude i negoziati di pace. Una proposta di legge antiterrorismo consentirebbe all’esecutivo di formulare una lista di gruppi terroristici e congelare i beni di chiunque collabori con loro. Secondo Elizabeth Dickinson dell’ong International crisis group, si tratta di politiche “del bastone e della carota”. Ma le organizzazioni per la difesa dei diritti umani temono che il leader colombiano possa usare il bastone anche per intimidire la società civile.

De la Espriella ha a disposizione fondi limitati per la sicurezza e altre operazioni. Il debito pubblico della Colombia, infatti, è pari al 60 per cento del pil. Senza un intervento, il governo prevede un disavanzo fiscale del 9,4 per cento del pil nel 2027. La situazione è così difficile che è in corso un dialogo con il Fondo monetario internazionale per concordare un prestito che potrebbe ammontare a 20 miliardi di dollari. Alla fine di ottobre il governo ha presentato una riforma fiscale e di spesa severa, che diminuirebbe il numero di beni ammissibili ad aliquote iva ridotte e speciali, amplierebbe la base imponibile dell’imposta sul reddito, taglierebbe il personale statale di un quinto e darebbe al presidente i poteri per ridurre la spesa con decreto. Le aliquote dell’imposta sulle aziende scenderebbero dal 35 al 31 per cento; i nuovi grandi investitori beneficerebbero di un’aliquota del 20 per cento per 16 anni. I conservatori in materia di fiscalità sono rimasti piacevolmente sorpresi. “Non è quello che ci si aspetterebbe da un populista”, ha sottolineato Mauricio Cárdenas, ex ministro delle finanze.

Far approvare la nuova legge non sarà facile. Il partito di De la Espriella può contare solo su una manciata di seggi in parlamento. Esiste una maggioranza filogovernativa solo sulla carta, ma il presidente dice di non voler ricorrere al consueto scambio di incarichi e risorse per ottenere sostegno politico. Rafael Nieto, senatore del partito di destra Centro democrático, accusa il governo di voler imporre le leggi invece di discuterle.

Valori tradizionali

Finora De la Espriella è sembrato poco incline al compromesso. A ottobre ha nominato come ministro dell’interno Alejandro Ordóñez, ex procuratore generale ultracattolico che da giovane bruciava i libri. La scelta è coerente con un’altra ossessione del presidente: realizzare una “controrivoluzione culturale” per ripristinare i valori tradizionali. De la Espriella ha fatto rimuovere dal museo nazionale decine di opere legate al femminismo, alla diversità sessuale e al processo di pace, e conclude i suoi messaggi con “Viva Cristo re”, nonostante gli avvertimenti dei tribunali sulla laicità dello stato colombiano. Forse spera che la guerra culturale galvanizzi la sua base in vista delle elezioni regionali dell’anno prossimo.

In questo e in altri aspetti segue l’esempio di Donald Trump. La Colombia è entrata a far parte dello Scudo delle Americhe, l’alleanza strategica guidata dagli Stati Uniti per combattere il narcotraffico nella regione. Washington ha già inviato a Bogotá diversi droni per dare la caccia ai criminali. Con il presidente statunitense De la Espriella condivide anche l’estrema permalosità, come dimostra il licenziamento del capo dell’istituto di statistica per aver affermato di non aver trovato prove che il governo Petro avesse manipolato i dati sul mercato del lavoro. I giornalisti critici con il governo hanno perso il lavoro. “C’è una tendenza autoritaria e populista di estrema destra”, dice Nieto.

Le piazze, intanto, si stanno scaldando. Circa 60mila manifestanti hanno preso parte alle proteste antigovernative il mese scorso. De la Espriella li ha liquidati come una “piccola minoranza che vuole fermare la Colombia”. Man mano che il numero dei manifestanti cresce, sarà più difficile mantenere questa linea. ◆ as

articles.preview: Il 17 novembre un attacco ucraino con missili e droni ha fatto crollare una sezione del ponte di Kerč (nella foto), che collega la Russia alla Crimea occupata, interrompendo il traffico stradale e ferroviario. Il presidente ucraino Volodymyr Zelenskyj ha rivendicato l’operazione, spiegando che è stata preparata e realizzata in varie fasi nell’arco di diverse settimane, spiega il Kyiv Independent. articles.body:
Il 17 novembre un attacco ucraino con missili e droni ha fatto crollare una sezione del ponte di Kerč (nella foto), che collega la Russia alla Crimea occupata, interrompendo il traffico stradale e ferroviario. Il presidente ucraino Volodymyr Zelenskyj ha rivendicato l’operazione, spiegando che è stata preparata e realizzata in varie fasi nell’arco di diverse settimane, spiega il Kyiv Independent. Poche ore prima Mosca aveva colpito due ponti sul Dnipro a Kiev. Secondo le autorità locali, nelle 24 ore precedenti gli attacchi russi hanno ucciso 14 persone e ne hanno ferite 78. Tra il 15 e il 16 novembre le vittime erano state invece almeno dieci e i feriti più di cento. I raid hanno preso di mira anche la rete energetica: nella regione di Dnipropetrovsk 700mila abitazioni sono rimaste senza elettricità. La Bbc rende noto inoltre che l’Ucraina ha accusato Mosca di aver volontariamente preso di mira, con un doppio attacco a distanza ravvicinata, i soccorritori intervenuti il 2 novembre dopo un primo bombardamento nel villaggio di Komyšuvacha. In quell’occasione i morti sono stati 72. Intanto la Commissione europea ha proposto per il 2027 un nuovo prestito di 45 miliardi di euro per Kiev.

articles.title: Xi, Trump and Putin hold unprecedented trilateral talks with Ukraine war, nuclear arms control on agenda
articles.summary: The meeting on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen was the first-ever three-way talks between the leaders of China, the United States and Russia.
articles.preview: The meeting on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen was the first-ever three-way talks between the leaders of China, the United States and Russia. SHENZHEN: Chinese President Xi Jinping and his US and Russian counterparts Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin held unprecedented three-way talks on Thursday (Nov 19), where they said they would discuss the war in Ukraine and nuclear arms control.
articles.body:
The meeting on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen was the first-ever three-way talks between the leaders of China, the United States and Russia.

SHENZHEN: Chinese President Xi Jinping and his US and Russian counterparts Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin held unprecedented three-way talks on Thursday (Nov 19), where they said they would discuss the war in Ukraine and nuclear arms control.

Seated around a big round table in a villa in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC), the leaders of the world's biggest nuclear powers took turns to give opening remarks.

"We are really making history," Trump said. "The three of us have a great deal to discuss.”

“No peace was ever forged by declining opportunities for engagement.”

Putin said the three countries have "numerous shared interests in the settlement of regional conflicts, including obviously the conflict in Ukraine".

Unlike Trump and Putin, Xi - who Chinese state media said was presiding over the meeting - did not make a reference to Ukraine, but said: "History tells us that when major powers live in harmony, the world is at peace. When major powers clash, the world falls into turmoil."

Xi said that their countries should work together to address global challenges, adding that they have a joint responsibility in maintaining peace and security.

In his opening remarks, Trump said the US, China and Russia are "uniquely positioned" to discuss reducing nuclear weapons.

“It’s not an easy thing to do - give them up,” Trump told Xi and Putin at the start of their meeting. The US president also said the three leaders would discuss the war between Russia and Ukraine.

Trump has insisted nuclear arms control be a central topic of the summit, despite China's repeated objections to joining talks with Washington and Moscow, which have far larger nuclear arsenals.

In his remarks, Xi said nuclear weapons should be comprehensively prohibited and completely destroyed, with the ultimate goal of building a world free of nuclear weapons.

A nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought, Xi said, according to China's official Xinhua news agency. He added that every effort must be made to prevent nuclear war.

Meanwhile, Putin told Xi and Trump that their countries can strengthen global stability if they cooperate constructively, adding that they should discuss global and regional issues as well as energy security.

The Russian leader said their three nations have a joint responsibility in maintaining peace and security.

This is the very first trilateral meeting between the three countries’ leaders. The afternoon talks, which lasted for around 90 minutes, took place at Kylin Villa, or Qilin Shanzhuang in Mandarin, a luxurious state-owned lakeside resort nestled in the hills of northwest Shenzhen.

Before the meeting, Trump had signalled that nuclear arms reduction and the war in Iran would be among his priorities, while the Kremlin had indicated that the war in Ukraine was its focus.

Beijing, meanwhile, had been relatively guarded about its priorities - saying only that the leaders would discuss safeguarding world peace and promote “strategic stability in major-power relations”.

Their meeting has drawn comparisons with the 1945 Yalta Conference between the US, Britain and the Soviet Union that formalised spheres of influence and set the stage for the post-World War II order.

It has also unnerved leaders of smaller economies, particularly in Europe and Asia, who fear the world's greatest military powers will disregard their interests.

But analysts have expressed low expectations of concrete breakthroughs as the leaders enter the talks with competing national interests and strategic priorities.

The gathering follows talks between Xi and Trump at the same venue earlier on Thursday.

In a meeting that lasted just over an hour, both men struck a positive tone as they sought to stabilise bilateral relations amid lingering trade and technology tensions.

Trump described Xi as a friend, saying they shared a “special relationship”. He also praised progress in balancing trade between the two countries, including fairer tariff arrangements.

Meanwhile, Xi said China-US relations were stable and improving, expressing willingness to work with Trump to keep ties on the “correct course”.

He also said the two countries have established a “new definition of a constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability, giving it new substance based on respect, fairness and reciprocity”.

articles.title: The unfolding Jensen Huang scandal: a timeline
articles.summary: Jensen Huang has resigned from Nvidia following an affair, which could have ramifications for national security as the U.S. and China race to develop the most advanced AI infrastructure.
articles.preview: Nvidia co-founder and now former CEO Jensen Huang has never been as prone to controversy as AI leaders like OpenAI’s Sam Altman or SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk. But the 63-year-old industry kingpin recently admitted that he cheated on his wife of 40 years in affairs that could have ramifications beyond Huang’s personal life and U.S. national security. U.S. officials believe that one of Huang’s likely romantic interests, Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, is a Chinese spy who has been feeding information back to Beijing.
articles.body:
Nvidia co-founder and now former CEO Jensen Huang has never been as prone to controversy as AI leaders like OpenAI’s Sam Altman or SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk. But the 63-year-old industry kingpin recently admitted that he cheated on his wife of 40 years in affairs that could have ramifications beyond Huang’s personal life and U.S. national security.

U.S. officials believe that one of Huang’s likely romantic interests, Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, is a Chinese spy who has been feeding information back to Beijing. (Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen, is of no relation to Jensen Huang.)

Megaspeed is a Singapore-based AI infrastructure company that reportedly purchased $4.8 billion worth of Nvidia chips over the last two years. The U.S. and Singapore have both previously investigated Megaspeed over suspicions that the firm was illegally sharing chips with China. The Justice Department has since taken over the federal investigation into the company, The New York Times has reported.

The story took a sudden turn on Wednesday. Citing five people who worked at Nvidia, the Times reported that Huang also had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, the company’s vice president of healthcare, who reports directly to him. Nvidia, Huang and Powell have not confirmed the report. Reached by a Times reporter, Huang reportedly said, “I don’t think you should be talking to me directly,” before hanging up.

By early Thursday morning, Huang was no longer CEO of the company he co-founded 33 years ago. Then, Thursday afternoon, Reuters dropped another bombshell, publishing a report alleging that Huang had yet another extramarital affair with another unnamed Nvidia employee.

The U.S. and China are embroiled in a fierce technological arms race to build the most advanced AI infrastructure, which could shape each country’s economic future, military prowess, and capacity for innovation. Nvidia is valuable in this competition as one of the world’s largest makers of AI chips, which are essential for accelerating AI development. But as an American company, Nvidia faces government restrictions on the sale of its most powerful chips to Chinese entities.

As the controversy unfolds, we are organizing the most relevant events into a reverse-chronological timeline to keep you up to date.

November 17, 2026: Nvidia posts strong quarterly earnings, says it does not plan to reinstate Huang

Nvidia reported its quarterly earnings on Tuesday, which beat Wall Street expectations with $115.8 billion in revenue, up 103% year-over-year. Despite the unknowns the company faces without Huang involved, interim CEO Colette Kress said that full-year revenue is also on track to exceed expectations. The company also plans to raise its outlook for the 2028 fiscal year, indicating confidence that this unexpected leadership change won’t get in the way of its trajectory.

“We have the best technologists on the planet with a world-class multi-year roadmap,” Kress said. “From a business perspective, it’s business as usual. We’ve engaged with our customers, we’ve engaged with our suppliers, our partners. They’re all 100% behind us.”

Nvidia chairman Harvey C. Jones affirmed that the company is not considering reinstating Huang. Kress also said that Nvidia will no longer sell its H200 chips in China, ending the company’s participation in a controversial loophole in the U.S. ban on the sale of advanced chips to the country.

November 17, 2026: Huang says he sees ‘outpouring’ of calls for him to return, says he ‘would be honored’ to return as CEO

Jensen Huang posted his first public statement since he admitted to having an extramarital affair more than a week earlier.

“Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company. If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO,” he wrote.

Many of Huang’s colleagues in the tech industry, including Elon Musk, Anduril founder Palmer Luckey, and Y Combinator President and CEO Garry Tan, have called for his return.

November 13, 2026: Huang was not confident in his successor, Colette Kress; reports describe Huang as ‘broken’

More reports continue to roll out that illustrate the shock and severity of Huang’s resignation from Nvidia.

Bloomberg reported that Huang looked “broken and shattered, his legendary energy depleted” by the time he surrendered his role on Wednesday night, uttering phrases like “whatever” and “I don’t care.”

Separately, The Wall Street Journal reported that Huang had been critical of his CFO and current interim CEO, Colette Kress. Huang is said to have described Kress as “a deer in the headlights” during a presentation this summer, and he had described Kress as someone who could not help him steer strategy or decision-making.

November 12, 2026: Democrats launch investigation into Nvidia; Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick summoned to testify before Senate Banking Committee

In a scathing letter sent to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, Representative Richard Neal (D-MA) and Senator Ron Wyden (D-OR) said they will investigate how the Trump administration handled Nvidia’s chip sales to China, especially after Trump was briefed about Huang’s relationship with a purported Chinese spy.

“Although [Lutnick] and President Trump were reportedly briefed on this intelligence, the Administration did not appear to acknowledge this evident national security threat. On the contrary: despite reportedly learning of Mr. Huang’s compromising relationship last fall, President Trump granted Nvidia permission to sell its advanced H200 AI chips to China in December 2025 in exchange for a cut of the export sales,” the letter states.

That same evening, Senator Tim Scott (R-SC) requested that Huang and Lutnick both testify before the Senate Banking Committee.

“The American people deserve answers,” Scott wrote on X.

November 12, 2026: Huang was having a third affair with another Nvidia employee, according to Reuters

After Huang was already ousted from Nvidia, we continued to learn more incriminating claims about the former CEO. According to Reuters, Huang had a third affair with an additional, unnamed employee of Nvidia.

November 12, 2026: Jensen Huang resigns, CFO Colette Kress named as interim CEO; Huang agrees to testify before Congress

Nvidia said its board had accepted Huang’s resignation on Wednesday. The company’s current CFO, Colette Kress, will take over as interim CEO while still fulfilling her CFO duties. Nvidia is expected to conduct a larger search to determine a permanent successor to Huang.

Harvey C. Jones, a managing partner of Square Wave Ventures and former CEO of Synopsys, was appointed as the company’s first-ever chair of the board of directors. Jones has been on Nvidia’s board since 1993.

Later in the day, Huang confirmed that he would testify in Congress at some point before Thanksgiving, which falls on November 26.

“Jensen and I have been very at odds as some of you already know on export controls, but Nvidia is a very important company to the United States of America,” House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast said to reporters. “I don’t want to see anything hurt in Nvidia, but he has some very serious questions to answer.”

The testimony is expected to take place behind closed doors, but Mast believes the briefing will be recorded and transcribed.

November 11, 2026: Nvidia’s stock drops as board reportedly preps to oust CEO Jensen Huang

After reports of a second extramarital affair, Nvidia’s board reportedly plans to meet to discuss Huang’s future at the company, per The Wall Street Journal. Stock fell about 8% in after-hours trading on Wednesday and is down 11% in the past five days.

Huang famously delegates very little and has about 60 direct reports, he has said. The company has not had an obvious successor or a succession plan.

November 11, 2026: Huang also had an affair with an Nvidia executive who reports to him, NYT says

The New York Times reported that Jensen Huang also had an affair with Nvidia vice president of healthcare Kimberly Powell, who reports directly to the CEO.

According to the report, Huang and Powell were captured on film “being affectionate” at a hotel during a conference earlier this year.

November 11, 2026: Congress plans to subpoena Huang to answer questions about affair

Huang has not responded to a request from three Republican congressmen to appear for a closed-door briefing for questioning about his affair with an alleged Chinese spy. House China Committee Chairman John Moolenaar said Wednesday on Fox Business that if Huang doesn’t agree to the briefing, he’ll likely be subpoenaed.

November 9, 2026: Huang pulls out of various speaking engagements

The Nvidia CEO pulled out of upcoming speaking engagements at the ElevenLabs Summit and Anthropic CEO Forum.

November 9-10, 2026: Details emerge about the business relationships between Nvidia and the alleged spy

Alice Huang and her family reportedly built a network of companies in China and Singapore to acquire Nvidia chips, including founding a Chinese company called Shanghai Century Litong. Founded in 2023, it became an Nvidia-preferred cloud partner, giving it priority access to chips, The Information reported. The Information also reported that Shanghai Century Litong facilitated buying $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia’s chips, including banned chips.

Nvidia’s head lawyer, Tim Teter, intervened in a 2025 U.S. government probe surrounding the suspected smuggling of AI chips by Megaspeed International, Bloomberg reported. Teter contacted Commerce Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler asking questions about whether the Trump administration played a role in detaining Alice Huang.

In early 2025, Alice Huang and a business partner sought China-based investors for an Asian data center, promising they had no problem in securing GPUs, the Financial Times reported.

November 8, 2026: Trump shows support for Nvidia CEO, calls him a “fine person”

On Sunday night, President Trump weighed in on Huang’s controversy and showed support for the Nvidia CEO.

“I have not spoken to him about it. I just know he’s a fine person, but you never know what’s going on,” Trump said.

When asked if Huang should remain chief of Nvidia, Trump said, “I think so. Oh yeah, sure.”

November 8, 2026: Huang admits to affair in public message to Nvidia employees; Nvidia board of directors begins investigation

Jensen Huang wrote in a letter to Nvidia employees — which was also published as a press release — that he cheated on his wife.

“I owe my family and all of you an apology,” Huang told his company. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”

Huang did not mention Alice Huang by name in the message, but linked his infidelity to “the national security concerns raised in news reports.”

“Nvidia’s Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America’s national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American,” Huang wrote.

Nvidia shares slid over 5% the following day.

November 5, 2026: Three Republican committee chairmen ask Huang for closed-door briefing

Three Republican congressmen — Chairman John Moolenaar of the House Select Committee on China, Chairman Brian Mast of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, and Chairman Rick Crawford of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence — sent a request to Huang for a closed-door joint briefing with their three committees.

“Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the [People’s Republic of China]’s access to sensitive U.S. technology and information,” the chairmen wrote. “The issue of PRC infiltration and access to cutting-edge U.S. technology is core to the investigative work of our three committees this Congress. It is vital that Congress determines the extent to which U.S. national security has been placed at risk.”

October 29, 2026: Jensen Huang publicly revealed to have developed ‘close relationship’ with suspected Chinese spy

U.S. officials had been investigating Alice Huang and Megaspeed for more than a year when the New York Times broke the story in late October that the two executives also had a close relationship.

An Nvidia spokesperson denied that this relationship was something out of the ordinary.

“Jensen’s interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected. Meetings with customers are part of a CEO’s job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year,” Nvidia spokesperson John Rizzo said. He added that “if the U.S. government believes that any person is a threat to American industry, it would let us know.”

Spring 2026: A secret memo circulates in the Trump administration about Nvidia CEO’s alleged relationship with Chinese spy

U.S. officials circulated a secret memo among policymakers that warned that Megaspeed’s Alice Huang, who had a relationship with Jensen Huang, was a spy for China’s Ministry of State Security. This memo was not public knowledge until it was later reported by the New York Times.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio supervised the drafting of the memo.

Late 2025: President Trump briefed on U.S. surveillance of Alice Huang and her relationship to Nvidia CEO but does not take action

Around the same time, per the New York Times’ report, U.S. President Donald Trump was briefed about intelligence findings that possible Chinese spy Alice Huang had formed a close relationship with Jensen Huang. Trump did not act on this information.

The Nvidia CEO, an ally of Trump, has repeatedly advocated for the U.S. government to let Nvidia expand its business in China.

October 2025: U.S. and Singapore each investigate Megaspeed over possible Chinese export violations

Megaspeed was confirmed to be under investigation by both the U.S. and Singaporean governments in October 2025. As a customer of Nvidia, Megaspeed was suspected of helping Chinese companies get around American embargoes on chip exports.

Megaspeed, a neocloud that used Nvidia chips, had been renting computing power to Chinese internet giant Alibaba and other Chinese companies, the Times reported. A Commerce Department official who had visited Megaspeed’s data center in Malaysia in 2024 had found a hoard of Nvidia equipment that was still packed in boxes and the concern was that this equipment was being directly shipped somewhere else, like China, rather than installed and sold as a cloud service.

Jensen Huang had been spotted socializing with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang as early as 2024 in Taiwan, where the Nvidia CEO was born.

These investigations into Megaspeed highlighted concerns about the degree to which Nvidia is able to track its chip exports. At the time, an Nvidia spokesperson told press that the company did not have “any reason to believe products had been diverted.”

“NVIDIA visited multiple Megaspeed sites yet again earlier this week and confirmed what we previously observed — Megaspeed is running a small commercial cloud, like many other companies throughout the world, as allowed by U.S. export control rules,” the Nvidia spokesperson said at the time.

articles.title: Anthropic vola all'esordio a Wall Street, vale 2.000 miliardi
articles.summary: L'esordio col botto crea nuovi miliardari. Brindano le banche
articles.preview: Anthropic dei record a Wall Street: le grandi attese sul primo test per l'intelligenza artificiale nell'era dopo Jensen Huang a Nvidia non sono andate deluse. La startup fondata solo sei anni fa ha infatti esordito col botto sul Nasdaq con il ticker 'Ant' superando SpaceX. I titoli hanno aperto a 111,50 dollari, in rialzo del 34% rispetto agli 83 dollari fissati in precedenza, per un valore di 2.000 miliardi di dollari, più di Meta e Tesla.
articles.body:
Anthropic dei record a Wall Street: le grandi attese sul primo test per l'intelligenza artificiale nell'era dopo Jensen Huang a Nvidia non sono andate deluse. La startup fondata solo sei anni fa ha infatti esordito col botto sul Nasdaq con il ticker 'Ant' superando SpaceX. I titoli hanno aperto a 111,50 dollari, in rialzo del 34% rispetto agli 83 dollari fissati in precedenza, per un valore di 2.000 miliardi di dollari, più di Meta e Tesla. Con il boom della quotazione, i sette fondatori di Anthropic - tutti ex dipendenti di OpenAI - diventano multimiliardari, arrivando a valere più di 20 miliardi ciascuno. A festeggiare sono però anche i dipendenti della società, che grazie all'operazione possono contare su una ricchezza media di 44 milioni a persona.

Grandi profitti anche per le banche che hanno curato l'ipo, con la quale sono stati raccolti 81,3 miliardi di dollari tramite la vendita di 980 milioni di azioni a 83 dollari l'una. Agli istituti infatti andranno complessivamente 550 milioni di dollari in commissioni, meno dell'1% del totale raccolto. Morgan Stanley e Goldman Sachs incasseranno complessivamente il 41% del totale, circa 110 milioni ciascuna. Cifre stellari che confermano l'appetito degli investitori per l'intelligenza artificiale nonostante le recenti difficoltà dovute allo scandalo di Nvidia e ai timori di una bolla che possa a breve scoppiare. Suonando la campanella dell'avvio degli scambi al Nasdaq, l'amministratore delegato Dario Amodei è apparso visibilmente emozionato e contento. "Non cederemo né alle pressioni commerciali né a quelle politiche", ha detto in un breve discorso assicurando che Anthropic resterà "ossessionata" dalla sicurezza dell'IA.

"Oggi mettiamo l'azienda in una posizione finanziaria più solida" e questo "rafforza ulteriormente la nostra determinazione ad agire nel modo giusto", ha spiegato Amodei, finito nei mesi scorsi al centro di uno scontro con il Pentagono sulle limitazioni all'uso dell'intelligenza artificiale che Anthropic aveva imposto, affermandosi come uno dei paladini dello sviluppo di un'IA sicura e che porti benefici a tutti. Il ceo di origini italiane - suo padre Riccardo Amodei era un artigiano pellettiere - è stato tra i primi a chiedere un rallentamento dello sviluppo dell'intelligenza artificiale e a mettere in guardia sui rischi di estinzione dell'umanità. Una posizione la sua condivisa anche da Elon Musk, che ha lodato la società.

"Conosco molte persone che ci lavorano, avendole incontrate ai miei tempi a OpenAI. Per quello che può valere, nessuno di loro mi ha fatto scattare il 'rilevatore della malvagità'", ha detto il patron di Tesla che ha un contenzioso aperto con Sam Altman, il numero uno di OpenAI. Il successo dell'ipo apre un nuovo capitolo nell'era dell'IA finora rimasta protetta dai riflettori finanziari, e arriva fra il crescente scetticismo degli americani nei confronti della nuova tecnologia. Le elezioni di metà mandato hanno infatti rivelato che gli elettori sono contrari ad avere data center nelle loro comunità e hanno paura degli effetti che l'IA potrebbe avere sul mercato del lavoro. Secondo il presidente della Fed Kevin Warsh, il fenomeno va esaminato da vari punti di vista. Da un lato può infatti aumentare la produttività del lavoro, con benefici ampiamente condivisi. Allo stesso tempo, comporta rischi di destabilizzazione legati a soggetti malintenzionati. Non si può inoltre escludere che l'IA deluda e che le aziende non riescano a realizzare rendimenti adeguati sui loro investimenti. Un'ipotesi che, alla luce dell'esordio di Anthropic a Wall Street, sembra per ora lontana.

articles.title: Anthropic’s IPO could deliver $156 billion to charity
articles.summary: At a stock price of $95, the frontier lab's Public Benefit Foundation, its employee donations, and the company's match tot up to $156 billion.

As you might expect from a company whose leadership emerged from the world of effective altruism (EA), Anthropic has multiple different avenues for cash raised in its market debut to be directed to philanthropy. First, the company’s Public Benefit Fund, or PBF (analogous to OpenAI’s foundation), was allotted 5% of the company’s shares, almost 850 million.
articles.body:
Anthropic’s blockbuster IPO has made quite a few people generationally wealthy, but it will also be an enormous windfall for the causes backed by the frontier lab and its employees.

As you might expect from a company whose leadership emerged from the world of effective altruism (EA), Anthropic has multiple different avenues for cash raised in its market debut to be directed to philanthropy.

First, the company’s Public Benefit Fund, or PBF (analogous to OpenAI’s foundation), was allotted 5% of the company’s shares, almost 850 million. At the current trading price of about $95, that will leave it with an endowment of $80 billion. And if the company continues its astonishing growth rate, Anthropic could add further 2% increases every time the company’s valuation grows more than 50% over the IPO price of $83, or about $124.50 per share for the next threshold.

The PBF’s money will be focused on research and activities related to increasing the benefit of artificial intelligence to humanity. The first commitment of the PBF was $200 million to study the impact of AI on workers; Anthropic has said it will consider donations to philanthropic organizations or “direct distributions to specific populations” — perhaps a hint of future UBI plans.

Anthropic also donated $50 million to the city of San Francisco last week. A company spokesperson tells TechCrunch the donation did not come from the PBF.

Next, Anthropic’s employees have pledged shares to philanthropic causes of their choice, and the company will match those donations 3-to-1 for longer tenured employees and 1-to-1 for newer ones. In its S-1 filing, the company said that it had reserved more than 550 million shares to fulfill pledges made before September 30.

Working backwards from that figure, and based on the disclosure that 84% of the shares were reserved for early employee matches, we can estimate that employees have pledged $23 billion of donations; the company’s match on those would be roughly $53 billion, depending on the stock price when those matches are delivered.

All told, it adds up to $156 billion — a huge amount of potential philanthropy. For context, Americans donated $617 billion to charity in 2025; if all of the pledged funds resulting from today’s transactions get to do-gooders, that will be equal to about a quarter of all U.S. donations made last year.

Employees will need to make good on their pledges for this to work out, and the value of the match will ultimately depend on when Anthropic makes its donation. The shares could also go to donor-advised funds, which would likely limit their initial impact.

Interviews with employees and institutions suggest that donors are most likely to support EA-inflected charities like Longview Philanthropy, GiveWell, Coefficient Giving, Foresight Institute, and Giving What We Can. And it seems likely that significant funding will be allocated to AI safety research, given the concerns expressed about that subject by many Anthropic employees.
